newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Former enemy Vietnam welcomes Clinton victory.
newsitem.headline: Former enemy Vietnam welcomes Clinton victory.

text.p: Former U.S. foe Vietnam welcomed the results of a presidential election on Wednesday showing victory for Bill Clinton, the man who normalised relations between Washington and Hanoi.
A Foreign Ministry spokesman said President Le Duc Anh would be sending a message of congratulations to his U.S. counterpart.
"We welcome Mr. Bill Clinton's win in the U.S. Presidential election," he said, reading from a prepared statement.

"On our side, Vietnam hopes the cooperative relationship between Vietnam and the United States will continue to develop for the benefit of the two countries and the benefit of peace, stability, cooperation and development in the region and world."
Hanoi and Washington normalised diplomatic ties in July 1995, two decades after the Vietnam War ended with the fall of Saigon to the forces of communist North Vietnam.
But relations since then have progressed slowly and the two countries have yet to achieve full trade and economic normalisation.

In an indication of the prevailing mood Wednesday's official Nhan Dan newspaper slammed U.S. radio station Asia Pacific Network -- formerly Radio Free Asia -- which is due to begin Vietnamese language broadcasts to the region next year.

"The true face of so-called American-style freedom has been exposed, a freedom to say bad words about countries which don't want to be imposed upon, a freedom to interfere in the internal affairs of other countries," it said.
